prerequisite: The drawing has a volume surface (base = existing ground, comparison = design) and a layer of closed boundary polylines
fixture_requirements: One TinVolumeSurface whose base and comparison surfaces both have geometry
>= 2 closed polylines on the boundary layer, at least one with an arc segment
At least one boundary containing both cut and fill (verifies cut / fill are both non-zero)
At least one boundary that is net cut overall (verifies a negative net is not swallowed to 0)
One boundary outside the volume surface extent (verifies it goes to warnings and the error carries the reason)
assertions: Read-only node: no Commit; drawing dbmod and file size are unchanged after the run

**Boundaries must be explicitly closed**: the first point has to be appended at the end, otherwise Civil throws ArgumentException 'Unable to calculate volume, possibly illegal bounding polygon'. close_ring defaults to true for exactly this reason

cut/fill must differ per boundary -- this is the key difference from calculate_surface_volume, which goes through GetVolumeProperties for the whole surface and returns N identical numbers for N boundaries
net == fill - cut, both per boundary and in the total
cut_adjusted == cut * cut_factor, fill_adjusted == fill * fill_factor
With inset > 0 the cut decreases monotonically (shrinking inward drops the outer ring of cut); use inset only when a boundary sits on the surface edge and returns nothing
Boundaries with arc segments are expanded by true arc length (reusing DredgeBuildRing), not by chord
When one boundary fails to return a volume it goes to warnings and the others are still computed; the batch is not aborted
When every boundary fails, throw; **the error message must carry the first failure reason**, not just 'see warnings' (warnings are lost on the throw path)
Throw when neither layer nor handles is given; throw and echo the count when nothing matched
When volume_surface is not a volume surface, add a warning saying 'this is not cut/fill' instead of reporting numbers silently
Two runs with the same parameters produce byte-identical results (read-only idempotence)

observed: 32 toe lines (5.5 m contours) against Surface1: outer boundary area 369,350 m2 in total, cut 71,037 / fill 424,240 / net 353,203 m3, 14 seconds, 0 warnings
With close_ring=false all 32 threw illegal bounding polygon -- closure is a hard requirement, not an option
Same boundary with inset 0 -> 0.5 -> 2.0: cut fell 1,243.87 -> 1,154.31 -> 946.53 monotonically, fill barely moved (the cut sits on the outer edge)
I20 net = -144 m3 (existing mean 8.65 above the 8.5 design top, net cut); the negative value comes through correctly
not_yet_covered: The branch that builds a volume surface from base_surface + comparison_surface (this run used the existing Surface1)
The branch where a boundary lies outside the volume surface extent
